entries.claim: two standing invariants join the project. First, every frozen artifact carries a byte-identity-after-rebuild test: rebuilding a month must leave every published bulletin, record page and outlook issue byte-identical, and only an explicit publish may write one. Second, no registered mechanism is wired until a test has made it fire: a code path that a registration describes but that no test has actually executed does not count as built
entries.note: both come from defects this project already produced rather than from principle. A reused outlook issue was silently rewritten by the monthly build, so display-only labelling leaked into an artifact that had been frozen for scoring; that is what the first invariant now forbids by test rather than by care. The scoring path could not resolve a claim on any instrument outside the founding seven, and the bust lamp's amber branch had never executed, both discovered only because a later stage forced them to run; that is what the second invariant now forbids. The invariants are recorded here so the tests that enforce them have a stated purpose and so a future stage cannot quietly drop one. Enforcement is by test, not by review.

entries.claim: from bulletin 002 onward each bulletin auto-registers its scoreable forward claims at publish, each as a pending auto entry with a maturity date and a resolution rule: one continuation claim per instrument whose three month continuation probability differs from 0.50 by at least 0.15, the risk lamp claim, and one synoptic persistence claim at three months while the banner gate is open
entries.note: definitions fixed here. Continuation probabilities are the current outlook issue's forecaster M at horizon three, read as the probability the instrument is still in its analysis state; the base month is that outlook issue's asof, so the stated probability and the resolution window refer to the same month, and the window is the base month plus three. The synoptic persistence claim reads forecaster M's synoptic distribution at horizon three the same way and is registered only while the synoptic gate is open. The risk lamp claim is unchanged and is per bulletin, since it is a statement about the bulletin's own month. Side is the side the stated probability commits to, above one half that the event occurs and below that it does not; exactly one half commits to nothing and registers no claim, which is why the 0.15 band exists for continuation claims. Deduplication, registered: a continuation or synoptic claim carries the quarter of the outlook issue it came from, and a bulletin does not re-register a claim of the same kind, node and outlook quarter that the chain already holds, because a forecast issued once must not be counted three times across the three bulletins of its quarter. Resolution reads the decoded state for the window month from the monthly decoder, and the synoptic claim reads the decoded synoptic series. Bulletin 001 is not backfilled.

entries.claim: the surface streak comprises published analyst calls only: bulletin claims scored at maturity, outlook quarter scorings, and live calls made in published bulletins. Development and qualification entries, meaning instrument checks, membership decisions, upgrade gates and falsified diagnoses, are excluded from the surface and render under their own labeled section, the laboratory record, on the record page. Retractions and revisions of published output remain on the surface as amber. By group string the surface is 'out of sample', 'corrections', 'bulletin claim scoring' and 'outlook quarter scoring'; every other group with a scored status is laboratory
entries.note: nothing is deleted and nothing is rescored. Under STREAK-DEF the surface held eight entries and read 1 hit, 3 misses, 4 null or corrected; those exact counts are preserved here so the change is auditable against what was published before it. Under this definition the surface holds three, B1, F1 and F2, and reads 1 hit, 0 misses, 2 corrected, while five entries move to the laboratory record: T1, T2 and T3, the three failed prediction upgrades, and N1 and N2, the two registered nulls. Rationale for the reclassification: those five were internal attempts to add a forecasting capability, tested and abandoned; none was ever published as a call to a reader, so counting them on a surface labelled as the analyst's record misdescribed them. The cost of the change is stated plainly: it removes three misses from the headline row, so the surface now reads better than it did, and the laboratory record exists precisely so that improvement is not a disappearance. Both totals render on the record page, the laboratory set renders in full most recent first, and the surface row links to it. Reclassification is a one-time redefinition registered before the render it governs; the group strings above are the definition and future entries are classified by them alone.

entries.claim: CAL-1 falsified the precondition of PERF-GOAL's calibration term. The confidences were already honest, so there was no improvement available to validate. At maturity that term scores as unsatisfiable by falsified precondition, not as underperformance, and the December verdict rests on the two forecasting terms, whose bars are unchanged
entries.note: the calibration term required a validated Brier improvement from the stage E upgrade. The audit found the printed confidences already close to honest and if anything slightly modest: mean printed 0.8382 against realized agreement 0.8553 over 6830 causal decodes across all 22 live instruments, with the decile curve tracking the diagonal. Isotonic recalibration therefore had almost nothing to correct and returned a relative Brier gain of 0.0013 against the registered adoption bar of 0.05, so CAL-1 was scored a miss and the recalibration was not adopted. This annotation records that the term's precondition, that the confidences needed correcting, is false. It does not move any bar, does not rescore CAL-1, and does not resolve PERF-GOAL, which stays pending until December. The two forecasting terms are unchanged: at the first outlook scoring a majority of instruments must show positive RPSS against climatology and must also beat persistence at the three month horizon

entries.claim: the recalibrated posteriors are adopted for displayed confidences if and only if the validation Brier score improves by at least 5 percent relative to raw
entries.note: not adopted. Validation Brier raw 0.09854 against calibrated 0.09841, a relative improvement of 0.0013, far below the registered threshold of 0.05. The isotonic map was fitted on 3769 causal decodes from 1998-01 to 2014-12 and validated on 3061 from 2015-01 to 2026-08, 6830 in total across all 22 live instruments. The reason there is nothing to fix: the printed confidences are already close to honest and, if anything, slightly under-confident. Over the whole audit the mean printed confidence is 0.8382 against a realized agreement of 0.8553, and the decile curve tracks the diagonal: 0.470 prints 0.461, 0.552 prints 0.558, 0.652 prints 0.638, 0.753 prints 0.720, 0.855 prints 0.885 and 0.962 prints 0.990. The check is scored a miss because its registered adoption condition was not met, not because the instrument failed: this is the first audit of any confidence number this system prints and it found them sound. Decoders are untouched either way

entries.claim: the public daily family chip appears only if DH1 and DH2 both hit
entries.group: D-HSMM public gate, registered before estimation
entries.note: gate shut: DH1 hit, DH2 missed at 38.76 flips per decade. The registered diagnosis is falsified. The chatter was attributed to the geometric sojourn of a vanilla hidden Markov model; an explicit negative binomial sojourn with a hard five-day minimum, fitted by EM to mean stays of 42 to 86 business days per state, produced more flips rather than fewer, and the MAP segmentation that cannot contain a short run still flips 33.39 times per decade. The instability is in the daily features, not in the duration prior. The daily clock question is closed for the year. GATE-G12 was not reopened and the storm watch lamp is untouched: the watch is an alert, the chip is a state, and no chip appears

entries.claim: the public streak renders scored forward-looking claims only. An entry is a dot if and only if its group is one of: 'out of sample', 'prediction upgrades', 'corrections', 'bulletin claim scoring', 'outlook quarter scoring'. The first three are the forward-looking claims already on the chain; the last two are reserved now so that future scorings are auditable against a definition fixed before the first render. Dot colour: green for status hit or oos, red for miss or fail, grey for null, un, ret or rev, hollow ring for pending. The row shows the last forty matching entries in chain order and the totals are taken over the whole matching set.
entries.note: excluded group strings, every one present on the chain at registration: 'held-out identification', 'graph nodes', 'graph edges', 'stage 6 audit', 'v2 wave 1, registered before estimation', 'transmission rewiring, registered before estimation', 'fix wave, registered before each run', 'phase A and B, registered before estimation', 'structural check, registered before computation', 'network membership checks, registered before estimation', 'network membership, rule: 2 of 3', 'tree leaf checks, registered before estimation', 'G12 daily instrument checks, registered before estimation', 'G12 public gate, registered before estimation', 'registered queue', 'registration, recorded before estimation', 'nervous system architecture', 'composition hierarchy', 'network population', 'operations, registered before first render'. These are registrations, joins, membership rules, held-out design checks, operational entries and unscored pendings, none of which is a forward-looking claim. At registration the matching set holds eight entries: one out-of-sample call, three failed prediction upgrades, two registered nulls and two corrections. The streak is therefore small and unflattering by construction, which is the point: it never reorders, never truncates misses and never omits nulls.
